memos.headline: S07 and S09 Lead in Relative Strength; S03 and S04 in Deep Downtrends to Avoid
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape across our universe today. S07 is the standout leader, sitting just -0.1% off its 52-week high with RSI at 73.5 and +37.8% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—parabolic but undeniably strong trend. S09 is the second-best chart, +15.2% above its 50d mean with +23.7% 12w relative strength and only -4.6% from highs, though RSI at 65 is more manageable. On the other side, S03 is deeply oversold at RSI 23.1, down -21.7% from highs, trading -13.7% below its 50d mean with -17.1% 12w relative underperformance—this is a broken chart, not a buying opportunity until it reclaims the 50d. S04 is similarly damaged at -26.0% drawdown, RSI 32.4, and -23.3% 12w relative weakness. I have moderate conviction in S01 as a defensive long given its +12.2% 4w relative strength, low ATR of 1.82%, and price sitting +8.7% above the 50d, though RSI at 70 warrants watching for a pullback entry.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names where earnings quality is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal leverage ($8.47B debt), while S04 posted a 47.3% net margin with net income surging +59.5% YoY on $81.27B of revenue. S05 also deserves attention: +18% revenue growth, 30.3% margins, and only $14.79B in debt make it a clean earnings story. On the other side, S02's net margin has collapsed to 2.1% with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for—and S09 is shrinking revenue (-5.2%) while net income falls 12.3%. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to positive revenue growth in S09 before reconsidering either name.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact With Moderating Growth: Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth and Staples Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a clear mid-cycle easing regime: the Fed has cut 75bp over the past year to a 3.75% upper bound, the 10y yield has fallen 48bp year-over-year to 4.04%, and the 2s10s curve has re-steepened to +62bp, all consistent with an orderly normalization. CPI is running at 2.7% y/y—still above target but not accelerating—while unemployment has drifted up 30bp y/y to 4.3%, suggesting a softening but not collapsing labor market. This backdrop favors duration-sensitive growth equities and defensive staples, while banks benefit from a steeper curve but face headwinds from slowing loan demand; cyclicals look vulnerable if the labor market deteriorates further. The regime call would flip if the next CPI print re-accelerates above 3% y/y or if unemployment spikes above 4.5%, either of which would force a reassessment of the easing path. I have moderate-to-high conviction in the growth/staples tilt and lower conviction on banks given mixed signals.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits most from falling yields and continued easing; 10y down 48bp y/y supports valuations.
Defensive staples outperform in a softening labor market with unemployment at 4.3% and rising; easing cycle provides a floor.
Banks gain from a steeper 2s10s curve (+36bp y/y) but slowing growth and rising unemployment temper loan growth outlook.
Cyclicals face headwinds as unemployment trends higher and the easing cycle signals the Fed sees growth risks ahead.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; moderate inflation and softening demand keep me sidelined pending clearer growth signals.
Growth-oriented names with duration exposure should re-rate as the market prices in further cuts from 3.75%.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S02 and S04 Washouts May Be Bottoming While S03 Joins the Negative Camp
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions across the universe as the primary sentiment signal this cycle. S02 suffered a brutal -19.6% one-day reaction on its Jan-27 results, and S04 dropped -10.0% on Jan-28; both moves are severe enough that negative sentiment is likely fully priced or oversold, creating potential mean-reversion setups if narrative tone stabilizes. S03's -5.6% drop on Feb-5 is more recent and the negative sentiment may still be developing, so I would wait for stabilization before getting constructive. On the positive side, S07 posted a clean +3.4% reaction on Jan-29 results and S01 gained +2.6% on Jan-22, suggesting constructive sentiment that has not yet become crowded given the modest magnitude of the moves. S08, S05, and S09 all had near-flat reactions (ranging from -0.5% to +0.6%), indicating sentiment equilibrium with no clear directional edge.

views.note: The -19.6% washout on Jan-27 earnings likely over-discounts negative sentiment, creating a contrarian entry if tone stabilizes.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges to Extreme Levels, Signaling Elevated Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic spike in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which at 438.29 is up 95.3% over three months and 55.6% over one month—levels consistent with major policy disruptions such as new sanctions, trade escalations, or export control regimes. The VIX at 20.82 (+37.7% 1m) corroborates rising risk premia, though HY OAS at 2.92% remains relatively contained, suggesting credit markets have not yet fully priced a structural shift. WTI crude at $63.08 (+6.2% 1m) is firming but not spiking, which tells me energy-supply disruption fears are present but not acute. Without specific GDELT event detail on sanctions or export controls, I have moderate conviction that the uncertainty is policy-driven (tariffs, China tech restrictions, or energy security measures) rather than a one-off shock, and I am positioning defensively on names with high geopolitical exposure while favoring domestically oriented or diversified names. A reversal in the EPU index below 300 or a concrete de-escalation announcement would change my view.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in five weeks suggest active corporate communication, possibly navigating policy changes; staying neutral until content clarifies exposure.
Two Reg FD disclosures in January amid surging policy uncertainty suggest the company may be managing geopolitical headwinds; I lean avoid until the EPU trend reverses.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in January are notable but without content detail I cannot determine if geopolitical exposure is material; neutral pending clarity.
Single Reg FD filing in early January; limited signal, but the macro backdrop of near-doubled policy uncertainty warrants caution.
One Reg FD disclosure late January; insufficient to assess geopolitical positioning, holding neutral amid elevated VIX and EPU.
No company-specific filings in evidence, and the extreme EPU/VIX environment argues against names where I lack visibility on geopolitical hedging.
With WTI firming at $63 and energy security concerns implicit in the EPU spike, energy-adjacent names may benefit if supply-chain policy tightens further.
